Although this class didn't teach much about Texas History, as long as you attended class and didn't procrastinate, an A was doable. You can chose out of 4 exams and 4 essays to do and opt out of 1 of each. She releases the exams questions and essay prompts a week before. She is very flexible, as she is disorganized and will often extend deadlines.

reviews.comment: Least favorite class I've ever taken. Very little (if any) learning about traditional Texas History, but HEAVY focus on racism all across United States. Exams are online and open-book, but are hyper-specific and difficult to perform well on without extensive prep. I did not learn anything useful that I needed about Texas History from this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Same person as last time (yes, this class was such a mess it's a 2-part review) but do NOT take this prof if you aren't a strong writer. And be prepared to take the most confusing, hyper-specific exams you'll ever take in your life.

I love to write and am liberal in my politics, but this class was still a trainwreck. The assignments are often confusing and lectures devolve into political rants. I learned almost nothing cuz of the structure and disorganization of this class. I try to give profs the benefit of the doubt, but I'm struggling to find good things to say tbh.

reviews.comment: By far the worst instructor I had in all of my 19 years of living. Believes that you are going there just to learn history, which is not the case for majority of us. I was once very sick (had doctor note), missed a pop quiz, but she would not let me make it up. I also missed information regarding an exam and she didn't put it on the rubric.
